stem: In this asthma action plan, when should you first recommend that the patient seek further medical attention?

options.text: See your doctor if you need Ventolin every 3 hours (or more often)
See your doctor if you need Ventolin every 2 hours (or more often)
See your doctor if you need Ventolin every 1 hour (or more often)

explanation: For a child with significant asthma symptoms, needing reliever more frequently than every 2 hours indicates poor control and the need for medical review. This option is the earliest threshold among those provided that appropriately prompts further medical attention.
rationale: The item is asking for the first advice point in an asthma action plan. Among the available choices, every 2 hours is the earliest appropriate threshold for seeking medical attention.

optionExplanations.A: This is less urgent than the threshold provided by the best answer.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Needing Ventolin every 2 hours or more often should prompt the patient to seek medical review.
optionExplanations.C: This indicates even more severe deterioration, but it is later than the first recommended review threshold among the options.

Instructions

Asthma Action Plan 1 - Muttley Magee

Muttley

Magee

is an 8 year old boy with asthma. He has had asthma attacks every month over winter and was discharged from the

paediatric

intensive care unit (PICU) a few days ago after a severe attack. He has been off oxygen since yesterday. He has also had a history of waking at night at least 5 days every week. He complains of wheezing with exercise and needs to take his

ventolin

at least once a day.
